title: Desilication Tank

introduction.definition: Pre-desilication tanks hold the bauxite slurry at about 95–100 °C for several hours so the reactive silica that dissolves re-precipitates as sodalite (desilication product, DSP) before digestion. This protects heaters from scale and keeps silica out of the product.
applications: Protecting digestion heaters from DSP scale
Controlling silica in pregnant liquor and product
key_points: DSP locks up caustic and alumina
introduction.summary: Pre-desilication tanks hold the bauxite slurry hot for several hours so dissolved reactive silica re-precipitates as sodalite (desilication product) before digestion. This protects heaters from scale and the product from silica.

temperature.title: Removing reactive silica before digestion
temperature.description: Kaolinite and other reactive silica dissolve in caustic liquor and would later precipitate as scale or contaminate the product. Holding the slurry at about 95–100 °C for several hours (often ~ 6–10 h) lets the silica re-precipitate as sodalite (desilication product, DSP), which leaves with the red mud. Each kg of reactive silica locks up caustic soda and alumina in DSP.

foundation: Ring-wall or slab foundation designed for full liquid/slurry weight plus agitator dynamic loads; settlement monitoring for large tanks.
alignment: Tank plumb and level; agitator shaft vertical and concentric; check gearbox mounting.
piping: Nozzles sized for slurry velocity (avoid settling and erosion); flush connections; scaling-resistant design and descaling access.
Caustic service: suitable materials, gaskets and spray shields; eyewash/safety showers nearby.
commissioning: Water trials (agitator run with water, check vibration and power); then caustic/slurry; verify levels, interlocks and spillage containment (bunds).

lubrication: Agitator gearbox oil and motor bearings per maker; no lubrication for static parts.

video_tutorials.title: Desilication Tank — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Desilication Tank.
Pre-desilication tanks hold the bauxite slurry at about 95–100 °C for several hours so the reactive silica that dissolves re-precipitates as sodalite (desilication product, DSP) before digestion.
This protects heaters from scale and keeps silica out of the product.
Typical applications include bauxites with reactive silica (kaolinite); protecting digestion heaters from DSP scale; controlling silica in pregnant liquor and product.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Desilication Tank: Agitator Shaft & Impeller.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Desilication Tank — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Desilication Tank.
Check temperature and agitator.
Descale coils and tank.
Agitator overhaul.
Watch for incomplete desilication: heater scaling downstream. Common cause: short residence, low temperature.
Watch for coil fouling: low temperature. Common cause: scale.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
